scope: Gateway withdrawal route binding, exposure limits, and release-build proof hardening
issue_fixed: Withdrawal requests stored the destination chain and X3 asset but not the exact route, so a release proof could select a different route with the same chain and asset. The route pending limit was never enforced, withdrawal releases bypassed the daily limit, and the settlement engine exposed a public dev-proofs feature that could compile the accept-all validator outside tests.
implementation: Bind every new withdrawal to the exact route selected at request time in a side map while preserving the existing withdrawal record encoding.
Fail closed for pre-upgrade withdrawals that have no exact route binding.
Validate route existence, enabled state, mode, destination chain, X3 asset, minimum amount, and maximum amount when a withdrawal is requested.
Include the route id in the domain-separated withdrawal id derivation.
Refuse release proofs and operational finalization through a different route, a disabled route, or a dry-run route.
Enforce pending_limit over burned but unreleased withdrawals.
Enforce a separate per-route daily withdrawal limit with rolling window reset.
Use checked supply and pending-counter subtraction and preserve collateral checks in one shared release settlement path.
Remove the dev-proofs feature; NoOpCrossChainValidator now exists only under cfg(test).
Bump gateway storage version to 2 and runtime spec_version to 26 while preserving historical withdrawal record decoding.

negative_and_boundary_tests: A request for an unknown, disabled, or dry-run route is refused.
A request whose chain or X3 asset disagrees with the selected route is refused.
A release proof naming another route with the same chain and asset is refused with WrongRoute.
A withdrawal created before exact route binding fails closed with WithdrawalRouteMissing.
A second burn above the route pending limit is refused without changing burned state or pending value.
A release above the route daily withdrawal limit is refused.
The release limit resets only after the configured daily window.
A mint or burn failure leaves gateway state retryable.
A second proof-id mint and a second withdrawal-id burn are refused.
limitations: This proves the on-chain request, burn, and release state machine with real dispatch and storage transitions; it does not prove a public-chain transaction.
The new gateway weights are conservative pre-regeneration bounds and still require FRAME benchmark generation.
No public Ethereum, Solana, or Bitcoin canary has moved value.
External audits, public testnet operation, and the production signer ceremony remain open.
